transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As Treasury Director, I'm calling this check-in to order. We have a $12,000,000 bond maturity payment scheduled for June 18, and our central liquidity reserve currently holds $16,000,000. The dashboard labels the full reserve as available for near-term funding, but before I can enter a binding release and execution plan, we need to complete our three-part check-in: liquidity, regulatory capital, and operations. This meeting must produce a same-day binding release and execution decision — deferral is not an option. So let's work through each area in turn. I'd like to start with liquidity: can someone report on our near-term liquidity position and any constraints on releasing funds from the reserve?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I confirmed this morning from the updated 30-day cash-flow forecast that the bank must retain exactly $9,000,000 to cover projected operating outflows, so no more than $7,000,000 of the reserve can be released.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a regulatory-capital constraint. I received a memo this week stating that $4,000,000 of the central liquidity reserve is treated as a ring-fenced liquidity buffer. For today's release plan, exactly $4,000,000 of eligible government securities must be transferred into the reserve as a mandatory securities substitution, regardless of which portion of the cash reserve is released. I should note this memo has not yet been added to the capital-policy register, but the requirement is binding for today's plan.
